description: Shared, extensible taxonomy for COSYgames. Category metadata is a starting point; level availability and individual content tags should be validated against each game's content before being treated as exhaustive.

cefrLevels.label: Pre-A1 / Beginner
cefrLevels.description: First words, recognition, and highly supported practice

cefrLevels.label: A1 — Beginner
cefrLevels.description: Simple familiar words and everyday phrases

games.name: 100 Questions

contentSets.name: Civic Exam
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source uses progressive content stages, not CEFR labels; no CEFR equivalence is asserted.
contentSets.audienceNote: Civic exam questions are country-specific and assume interest in civic knowledge; adapt region settings and review for learner context.

contentSets.name: Questions to Family
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source progresses from daily life to deeper relationships; these stages are not CEFR assessments.
contentSets.audienceNote: Source provides a children-friendly card side and an adult-friendly side; choose the side appropriate to the group.

contentSets.name: Questions to Friends
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source progresses from safe icebreakers to more personal topics; stages are not CEFR assessments.
contentSets.audienceNote: Prompts become personal and include relationships, boundaries, and conflict; preview for younger groups.

contentSets.name: Interview Questions
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source uses interview stages, not CEFR labels; language demands vary by role and answer.
contentSets.audienceNote: Interview and workplace prompts are best suited to learners ready for career-related discussion.

contentSets.name: Questions to Myself
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source contains multiple themed progressions; no CEFR equivalence is asserted.
contentSets.audienceNote: Source provides a children-friendly card side and an adult-friendly side; choose the side appropriate to the group.

contentSets.name: Netflix Documentary Questions
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source uses narrative stages and media themes, not CEFR labels.
contentSets.audienceNote: Media/documentary prompts may refer to mature themes; preview the selected questions and source material.

contentSets.name: Questions to Students
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source uses progressive topic stages, not CEFR labels; audience suitability is separate from proficiency.
contentSets.audienceNote: Source provides a children-friendly card side and an adult-friendly side; choose the side appropriate to the group.

contentSets.name: Teacher & Student Questions
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: The source uses themed stages and humour; no CEFR equivalence is asserted.
contentSets.audienceNote: Teacher-student framing can be used across ages, but select questions and humour for the actual group.

games.audienceNotes: Audience suitability depends on deck and card side. The Family, Student, and Myself decks explicitly provide a children-friendly side and an adult-friendly side. Other decks may contain personal, sensitive, civic, or adult-oriented prompts; do not treat the game-wide audience tags as blanket approval for every deck or question.
games.modeNotes: The game supports individual and group lesson types. The UI says both players or the whole group can answer; solo mode should be treated as self-reflection/teacher-led preparation rather than a verified standalone game mode.

games.name: Story Chain
games.audienceNotes: The activity is collaborative storytelling with sentence-by-sentence contributions. Audience suitability depends on the selected language, vocabulary pool, and facilitator support; the interface does not provide age-specific content filtering.
games.modeNotes: Collaborative chain-building naturally supports pairs and groups. Solo use may be possible for practice, but the game description frames it as collaborative rather than a verified solo-first activity.

games.name: Story Weaver
games.audienceNotes: The built-in grammar curriculum begins at A1 and progresses through higher levels. Story themes and examples should still be previewed for the intended age group; the interface is English-only.
games.modeNotes: The curriculum provides prompts and grammar cues for composing stories; pairs and groups can share the storytelling task, but the setup does not enforce a particular group size.

games.name: Hot Seat
games.audienceNotes: The setup describes one player guessing while others give clues. Preview vocabulary and definitions for the intended age group; proficiency selection is not an age-suitability guarantee.
games.modeNotes: The rules require at least a guesser and a clue-giver, with others able to watch or contribute; pairs and larger groups fit the described roles. The game uses a 60-second timer and 15 rounds.

games.name: Action Hero
games.audienceNotes: The activity asks players to act, mime, describe, or use sound effects for teammates to guess. The interface has no age-specific content filter; review vocabulary and acting prompts for the learners and group context. Movement can be adapted for accessibility.
games.modeNotes: Team-based guessing is the described format, with a player acting and teammates guessing. Pairs and larger groups are plausible; the setup does not enforce a specific minimum or maximum player count.

games.name: Identity Mystery
games.audienceNotes: The game uses hidden identities across famous people, jobs, and nationalities. Suitability depends on the chosen category and language data; review culturally specific names and nationality-related content for the group. No age-specific filter is provided.
games.modeNotes: The player asks or records descriptive clues/questions to uncover a hidden identity. The UI does not set a fixed group size; pairs and groups can use it as a collaborative guessing activity. Do not assume solo play is a distinct supported mode.

games.name: Object Quest
games.audienceNotes: The activity reveals hidden scene objects and target nouns. Suitability depends on the selected vocabulary, language data, and accessibility needs; the setup does not provide age-specific content filtering.
games.modeNotes: The game is a visual object-discovery activity and may be used individually or collaboratively, but the setup does not define player roles or enforce group size. In-person availability does not by itself guarantee offline operation.

contentSets.name: Core concrete vocabulary links
contentSets.sourceLevelNote: Most built-in English puzzles do not carry an explicit level field; do not assume they all belong to a CEFR band.

games.name: Emoji Odyssey
games.audienceNotes: Offers Guess and Story modes. Guess mode requires enough emoji-tagged vocabulary for the selected language and level; Story mode is a separate fallback when that vocabulary is unavailable. Review emoji meanings and story prompts for cultural context and age suitability.
games.modeNotes: The setup provides Guess and Story modes but does not enforce group size. Both can be adapted for individual practice or collaborative classroom play; treat those as facilitation choices rather than enforced player-count rules.

games.name: Lucky Numbers
games.audienceNotes: The source offers a Caller role for a group and a Player role for solo play or play with a host. The alphabet and number ranges are explicit practice sets; they are not ordinary CEFR vocabulary bands. Select the range appropriate to the learners and language.
games.modeNotes: Supports a Player role (solo or with a host) and a Caller role for a group. The selectable practice sets are Alphabet, Numbers 0–9, Numbers 0–19, and Numbers 0–99. The source fetches number words online with numeric fallbacks, so in-person use does not guarantee internet-free operation.
